findings.title: Live training video sessions dropped for head-office users (root cause: customer TLS-inspecting proxy)
findings.description: Head-office users reported that in-browser live video training sessions would connect, start, and then die mid-call, sometimes reconnecting and sometimes not; remote mine-site users on satellite/cellular links were unaffected. Diagnosis found the customer's corporate TLS-inspecting security proxy was decrypting/re-inspecting traffic and mishandling the websocket upgrade and long-lived connection used for the sessions, terminating it after a while. The customer's network team whitelisted BetterBark's session domains from TLS inspection, and the customer confirmed zero drops for a full week afterward. Both sides explicitly agreed the platform behaved as designed and the fix was entirely a customer-side network configuration change, so no product defect was logged.
findings.quote: That's what came to me. "The video keeps cutting out." Which is the least useful bug report in the world, but that's what I had to start with.
findings.severity_reason: While active it fully blocked a core real-time feature (live coaching sessions) for an entire office location with no client-side workaround, but the cause was confirmed to be the customer's own network appliance, it was fully resolved via a customer-side config change, and it has been stable for a verified week, so there is no ongoing product risk.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue involves websockets/TLS-inspection proxies; distinct from PROJ-101 (report timezone) and PROJ-138 (Outlook ICS) which are the only other session/reporting-timing items in the catalogue. Explicitly closed as customer-side, not filed as a product bug.
